CVE-2026-110337.title: CVE-2026-110337 CVE Record
CVE-2026-110337.description:
The Strava datasource plugin's resource handler POST /strava-api forwards a client-supplied endpoint string, and its query parameters, to the Strava API (https://www.strava.com/api/v3/<endpoint>) without validation.

When the datasource is not in OAuth pass-through mode, the request is made with the access token stored on the datasource, not the caller's identity. Grafana authorises plugin resource calls only on the datasources:query permission, which Viewers have by default. Any such caller could therefore request any Strava API path the connected account's OAuth grant allows, for example athlete/clubs or routes/{id}, and read the response.

The plugin's frontend (stravaApi.ts) only needs a fixed set of paths: athlete, athlete/activities, activities/{id}, activities/{id}/streams and segments/{id}.

Requests to Strava are GET only, so the issue is read-only.

Affected: plugin versions 1.2.0 through 1.7.2. The fix restricts endpoint to those five patterns and is pending release. The…

CVE-2026-125333.title: Forge: ReDoS in forge.http response header and cookie trimming
CVE-2026-125333.description: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. A malicious server or on-path attacker can supply a long whitespace run followed by a non-whitespace character in a response header, causing response.readHeader() or response.getCookies() to repeatedly scan the input and block the Node.js event loop or browser tab for minutes. Applications are affected only when they use forge.http with a socket pool to communicate with an untrusted server; forge.http is not loaded by require('node-forge'), and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

CVE-2026-134047.title: Open Robotics RViz IntensityPCTransformer PointField Out-Of-Bounds Read Denial-of-Service Vulnerability
CVE-2026-134047.description:
Open Robotics RViz IntensityPCTransformer PointField Out-Of-Bounds Read Denial-of-Service Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of Open Robotics RViz. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the IntensityPCTransformer handling of PointCloud2 messages. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a read past the end of an allocated object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create a denial-of-service condition on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-32645.

CVE-2026-137280.description: The Dashboard Widgets Suite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'dws-notes-user[note]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. CVE-2026-99274.title: smb: client: fix fiemap wild read on empty truncated response
CVE-2026-99274.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix fiemap wild read on empty truncated response

smb3_fiemap() treats -E2BIG from SMB2_ioctl() as a truncated range blob
and loops for the next chunk. If the server reports
STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW with OutputCount == 0, SMB2_ioctl() returns
-E2BIG with out_data == NULL and out_data_len == 0, and the existing
length checks accept the empty result. The loop then evaluates

next = out_data[num - 1].file_offset + ...

with num == 0, reading 16 bytes before NULL.

Reject a truncated range blob that contains no range, so the resume
offset is never computed from an empty response. Also require the last
range in a truncated blob to advance the resume offset without
overflowing, and to stay within the requested range; a malicious or
broken server could otherwise make no progress or underflow len and loop
forever. Free the previous response buffer before retrying.

Reproduced on 6.6.87.2 with a malicious SMB2…

CVE-2026-99429.title: ocfs2: pin refcount trees before dropping the lookup lock
CVE-2026-99429.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin refcount trees before dropping the lookup lock

A refcount tree returned to ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree() must stay alive
until that caller releases its operation reference. However,
ocfs2_get_refcount_tree() returns the cached pointer after dropping
osb_lock, and the caller only takes its kref afterwards. The registry
reference does not protect this gap from concurrent removal.

This can happen when another node frees a refcount root and reuses its
block with a different generation while this mount retains the old
cached tree. Two local operations on different inodes sharing the new
root, such as data CoW and an external xattr update, can then look up
the same stale tree. Their inode locks are independent, and both the
REFCOUNT DLM lock and rf_sem are acquired after the first operation
reference.

CVE-2026-99560.title: wifi: mt76: mt7925: fix reset panic caused by the WM2 rx irq mask
CVE-2026-99560.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mt76: mt7925: fix reset panic caused by the WM2 rx irq mask

mt7925_irq_map sets wm2_complete_mask, but mt7925_dma_layout has no
tx done ring, so the MT_RXQ_MCU_WA queue and its NAPI are never set up.
On a chip reset, mt7925e_mac_reset() calls napi_disable() on that NAPI
and crashes:

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000a40
Workqueue: mt76 mt7925_mac_reset_work [mt7925_common]
RIP: 0010:mutex_lock+0x1c/0x50
Call Trace:
napi_disable+0x1d/0x50
mt7925e_mac_reset+0x327/0x420 [mt7925e]
mt7925_mac_reset_work+0x9a/0x1a0 [mt7925_common]

Remove the WM2 mask from mt7925_irq_map and from
MT7925_INT_RX_DONE_ALL.

CVE-2026-99678.title: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent
CVE-2026-99678.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent

xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks for the whole count in an
unsigned int. For a pNFS layout the client chooses that count, and an
RW LAYOUTGET for 16 TiB wraps the reservation and shuts XFS down.

xfs_bmapi_write() maps at most XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN blocks here, so cap
the count at that. nfsd asks again for the rest. The other callers get
the same mapping as before.
